common.environment: Chromium on an Apple-silicon MacBook Air, everything in-browser

image-compressor.note: Default settings, MozJPEG encoder. No visible difference at 100% zoom on the sample.

image-resizer.note: Lanczos resampling via pica, with dimensions set to 1600 px wide.

heic-to-jpg.sample: a 2.3 MB HEIC of the same photograph
heic-to-jpg.result: 2.3 MB HEIC → 2.4 MB JPG in 5.7 seconds
heic-to-jpg.note: JPG is usually larger than HEIC at like-for-like quality - HEIC compresses better. Convert for compatibility, then compress if size matters.

webp-converter.result: 3.4 MB JPEG → 1.2 MB WebP (64% smaller) in 3.1 seconds

png-to-jpg.result: 66 KB PNG → 624 KB JPG - larger, not smaller
png-to-jpg.note: Honest caveat: JPG is built for photographs. Flat graphics with sharp edges are already near-optimal as PNG, and converting them to JPG grows the file. Convert photos, keep graphics as PNG.

compress-pdf.sample: a 6.6 MB, 2-page image PDF built from the test photograph
compress-pdf.note: Pages are re-rendered and re-encoded with MozJPEG. The output is returned unchanged if compression can't beat the original. Text-first PDFs compress far less - they're already small.

merge-pdf.sample: two copies of the 6.6 MB image PDF
merge-pdf.result: 13.2 MB in → 13.2 MB out (lossless) in 1.0 second
merge-pdf.note: pdf-lib page copy: merging never re-encodes or degrades pages.

audio-compressor.sample: a 10-second 44.1 kHz WAV music clip (1.7 MB)
audio-compressor.result: 1.7 MB WAV → 157 KB MP3 (91% smaller) in 0.8 seconds
audio-compressor.note: lamejs MP3 encoding at the default bitrate, entirely in the browser.
